contexts.text: The learned... who desire to speak cautiously, say that there is a certain supreme Being, they know not what, that rules all things.
If such were asked whether they know what no proprium is, they would say that it is no being, and that if they were deprived of proprium they would be nothing.
This is general with all nations, for everyone acknowledges some highest Being when he beholds the universe...
It is most false, and, as it is called, an entity of reason, to say, that...

They who divide this Trine which is in one are none but those who say that they acknowledge one supreme Being, the Creator of the universe, which is excusable in those who are out of the Church. But those within the Church who say so, do not acknowledge any God whatever, although they say so, and sometimes suppose so; still less do they acknowledge the Lord.
All those within the Church who say that they believe in a supreme Being, and hold the Lord in slight estimation, are they who believe nothing whatever...

They who ascribe each and all things to their Own sagacity, and say that there is a supreme being which rules something in general... but nothing in particular, and who have confirmed themselves in this opinion, are also of the same character. Described.

They who say that they acknowledge a supreme being, of which they have no idea of perception, for the most part acknowledge no God, but nature in the place thereof... Very many of the learned among Christians are of this character...

Under the left foot, a little towards the left, are such as have attributed all things to nature, and still have confessed a Being of the universe from whom are all things which belong to nature. But examination was made as to whether they believed in any Being of the universe, or highest deity, which has created all things; and, from their thought communicated to me, it was perceived that it was an inanimate affair with no life in it in which they had believed; from which it was evident that they did not acknowledge a Creator of the universe, but that they acknowledged nature...

When (the rational natural man) beholds nature and the order of things, he sees that nature is a complex of means, and then perceives that an intelligent supreme Being has arranged them... But a sensual man does not comprehend that anything distinct from nature can exist, thus neither any being which is above nature.
Within the Church are very many such, who deny the Lord, and say that they acknowledge a supreme Being.
All in Hell think against the Lord... and yet very many say that they acknowledge a supreme Being, by which they mean the Father...
When (the Ancient Church) thought about Jehovah they did not think as of a universal being, of whom they had no idea, but of the Divine Human...

But they who say that they believe in an invisible Divine, which they call the Being of the universe, from which all things have come forth, and reject the faith concerning the Lord, have been found to believe in no God...
Thoughts, etc. are not entities flying and flowing out of nothing...
They would be a mere entity of reason, which, in itself, is not anything.
Abstracted or separated from them they are nothing but entities of reason...
From an entity of which nothing can be predicated, nothing can be made by massing.
Divine attributes... separated from a Man, are pure entities of reason.
The name Jehovah... means the supreme and only Being, from which is everything...

In order to separate God from nature, some have devised a most universal something which they have called the Being of the universe; and as they know nothing more about God, this Being is with them an entity of reason, which means nothing.
Unless being is substance, it is an entity of reason, for substance is being standing firm.
Although the human mind can acknowledge... that the first being, or the first Being is infinite, still it cannot Know what is its nature...
Nor is form any abiding being except from essence...
What then is your act, except a purely ideal thing, which is called an entity of reason?
